question: Which authority decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Speaker of Lok Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The **Speaker of Lok Sabha** has the exclusive authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill as per **Article 110** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• A Money Bill is primarily concerned with matters such as taxation, borrowing by the government, expenditure, and financial obligations of the state.
 
• The Speaker’s decision regarding the classification of a Bill as a Money Bill is considered final and cannot be challenged in any court.
 
• The **Money Bill** can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the Presid
